finalText:
Drafted into `CHANGELOG.md:3`. Here's what I found and how I got there.

**The shape of the history:** 380 commits, and by type — 153 chore, 73 refactor, 64 test, 33 ci, 20 docs. That's 343 commits with zero user-visible effect. The actual signal is **1 feat, 26 fixes, 10 perf**. The merged-PR sheet is a subset of the same commits (it stops at #4246 / 2026-06-17), so it added nothing the log didn't already have — I cross-checked every feat/fix/perf in it against the log.

**Collapsing the duplicates matters here.** The same fix title lands in three or four modules — "guard the null cursor in the paginator" appears in api, db, queue *and* webhooks; "duplicate header" in core, http, billing. Those are separate commits but one thing a user notices, so 26 fixes became 10 lines.

Three judgment calls worth your attention:

1. **The 401/403 change is breaking** and nobody labelled it as such — it's a plain `fix(auth):`. Anyone branching on the status code to trigger a token refresh breaks silently. I put it under Breaking.

2. **Two more may be breaking**, and I did *not* decide for you — they're a VERIFY comment block in the file. Dropping the "unused" v1 export route is only safe if it was genuinely unreachable; "unused" in a commit message usually means "we don't call it," not "no installer calls it." Same for the internal error types that stopped being re-exported across five modules — if those names were importable, that's a compile break for TS consumers. Both need a check against the published surface before you ship.

3. **The latency histogram units fix is user-visible in an unusual way** — it's a bugfix, but it silently changes recorded values, so anyone with a dashboard on that metric will see a step change on upgrade. I called that out in the bullet rather than burying it.

**What I left out, deliberately:** all 10 perf commits. Your template has three headings and no Performance section, and not one of the perf commits carries a measurement — "skip the JSON round-trip on the hot path," "avoid the extra clone in the mapper." Unquantified perf claims in release notes are noise at best. If you want them, the honest version is a single line like "Assorted performance improvements to request serialization and the database layer," which I'd rather you approve than assume.

Also skipped: the dependency bumps. All runtime deps (undici, pg, knex, ioredis, fastify, zod, pino, nanoid, dotenv) moved by patch or minor only — nothing an installer notices.

One loose end I couldn't resolve from the log: there are four `docs: note the minimum node version` commits plus CI moving to Node 22 and `.nvmrc` pins. That pattern usually accompanies a minimum-Node bump, but I saw no unambiguous `engines` change — the `package.json` edits in those commits are indistinguishable from the field-sorting churn. Worth a look at `package.json`; if the floor did move, that's a Breaking bullet.
